learning_objective: 🎯 Let us use charts and graphs to count, compare, and learn mathematical facts about our amazing wild animals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A bar graph uses long blocks (bars) to show numbers. The taller the bar, the bigger the number! We can draw bars to show how many elephants or tigers live in a forest.
By looking at charts, we can easily see which animal is the most in number and which is the least. We just look for the tallest and shortest lines!
We can use animal charts to do math! We can add the bars to find the total animals, or subtract a short bar from a tall bar to find the difference between them.

fun_activity.title: 📊 My Favourite Animal Graph
fun_activity.instructions: Ask 5 family members or friends what their favourite wild animal is. Make a small chart and color a block for each vote!

quick_recap: ⭐ Bar graphs use rectangular blocks to show us data clearly.
⭐ A tall bar means a bigger number, and a short bar means a smaller number.
⭐ Charts help us easily add, subtract, and compare different groups.
